items.note: N0 states the signed exchange (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a), the bit-case swap and restoration of every scratch wire; N0.1-N0.4 follow the proof at 741-765 (net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c; central coefficients |S cap T| mod 2 and (|S cap T|-1)/2 cancelled by the side injection; the three-stage chain). Not carried: h=100, the exact neighbour rules (only implied by N0.2/N0.3) and the wire counts W_b, W_c of 767-782, which lie outside the lemma itself.

F0 gives D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, with edge changes D_v D_u^{-1}. F0.1-F0.4 reproduce the invariant: sources by definition, edges by the edge operator, gates because a common frame commutes with a pointwise linear gate, and the signed route epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on all roles. This is the paper's argument at 804-825.

Everything in the statement is present: nondegenerate labels in F^{tensor 3} of dimension m=h^3, the pairing |S cap T|-1 over Q and the dot product over F_2, nested labels, central edges 3->4 as the only decreases (each losing h), L=Ich, Wm-2N+2L, and 100/539, 101/539. R0.1/R0.2 derive the budget and L0.2/L0.3 the interstage and side-wire nesting. But the key claim about decreasing edges is only restated (L0.4 quotes the lemma), not derived. Missing are the gate-label table eq:motif-labels (A tensor F on X-center, B tensor F on Y-center), the residual table (1021-1043) and the argument for binary orthonormal bases (1073-1102).

B0 matches Proposition prop:bit-motif-interface: XOR gates, permutation rho, M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m, and s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m. B0.1-B0.4 follow the proof at 1156-1172: rank(P_V - P_U) = dim change, the N exceptional edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one, the deficit N-2L_b, and the endpoint identity. K0.2 supplies the shear frames Phi_M and the resulting H <- H+D.

P0 gives one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c < W_c m, and C^{tensor m} on every role. P0's own wording omits the diagonal corrections, but P0.6-P0.8 supply them (C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates, Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}, the sign undo). P0.1-P0.3 reproduce weight additivity mod 4 and the Hadamard conversion, following 1231-1315. The explicit formula for C_U and the k-column tensoring are only implicit (the latter appears in Y0).

Present: L<N/2 via 100/539 and 101/539, the deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0, and B0.5's chain (deficits above 20*2^{-50}, m<2^20 so log m<20, m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-20*2^{-50}) > m(1-eta)) giving s/W < m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. The exact values of eta_b and eta_c are not given, but the comparison the paper actually uses is.

S1.1 states the four elementary operations correctly. S1.2 drops the hypothesis that the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time (566). It also explains the unit-multiplication case by the one-piece split-and-merge of a shift, but the paper uses a c-way split and a stack reversal for that case (592-614). There is no derivation.

T0 and MS0 state both lemmas exactly. T0.1-T0.3 follow the pivot elimination: topmost row, rightmost entry, active indices, one rank-one block per step. MS0.1-MS0.4 follow the choice of prime, the O(V) triangular transforms in descending order, the conjugation order, and the three-step realization of each one of Pi with a single interchange.

Every step of the proof at 1491-1616 is present: the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} by recursive interchanges, the frame identity giving Phi_{I_m}, H <- H+D on every row including scratch rows, the three-shear swap, s calls, the recurrence F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with its geometric-sum cases, and the O(V) fixed-tape parking schedule. K0's hypothesis names only s<Wm; the endpoint half of eq:finite-shear-contract appears in B0/K0.2.

S1 states O(Vu^tau) for arbitrary prefix, gap and suffix. S1.4.1-S1.4.6 follow the proof: k and rho=O(log 2e), high digits joined into a row field R=q^{2 rho} >= W^k, padding to R'<2R, the base-m pieces summing to O(Ve^tau), binary padding to [q^e], and the widths that differ by one bit.

Y0 gives exactly s_c children on e/m axes plus a fixed number of row additions. Y0.1-Y0.5 reproduce eq:phase-edge-coordinate via P_M, eq:phase-inverse-child, the m(m-1)+3m row additions, the s_c count, and eq:phase-butterfly-layer, as at 1855-1931.

Present: the eight conditional additions and their result, the per-line cyclic shifts, the guard interval [10, 2^{K-1}-11], delta_bad = min{1, 80(f-1)2^{-K}}, the fact that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes the bad set, the radix-sort repair, the full time bound, and the application to row additions (2210-2231). A0's asymptotic regime omits the condition f <= d <= p (2008).

Z0.1-Z0.10 follow 2253-2448 step for step: leaf cost O(Ve), node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), q_0 row chunks padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}, children of volume V/W, F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), overhead O(e^lambda), internal and leaf sums, the base-m pieces, and O(d^{lambda'}).

B0x states H_0^{tensor D} on one common bit per chunk with a single truncation in O(Vd^{lambda'}); B0x.1 adds the error < sqrt2 2^{-p} and the disk bound. G0-G0.5 reproduce the guard bound: A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E with E=64(W+m+1)^3, depth <= C_0 d^{C_1}, values at depth j in 2^{-(p+j)}Z[i] with modulus <= 2^j, and Delta=o(p). The proof combines the phase, packed and recurrence pieces as at 2686-2758. B0x's method misdescribes the child count (see errors).

C1 and C2 state the character cancellation, B_t F_t^- and F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, the layout L, the error sqrt2 ell 2^{-p} and the cost O(Tp[dK + pK^{tau-1} + ell d^{lambda'}]). The sub-steps follow 2819-2915 (index shift by t/2^{v+1}, DIF, bit reversal, the reverse traversal, grouped rounds) and 2990-3199 (prefix slots, Dq-1 exchanges, per-round layer calls, monomials, the truncation commuting with J_E, the order LB).

C3 states the lemma. The sub-steps reproduce B_0=2^{4p}, the four products from the established multiplier, the separation |h_j| <= r2^{2p} < B_0/2, two's-complement evaluation with carries in {-1,0}, centered extraction with carries in {0,1}, the negacyclic reduction, and the truncation by p+ell bits.

C states the error sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p} and the cost. C.1-C.7 follow the proof: the normalization identity, P(LBu,LBv) = LB P(u,v), the error chain 2delta, 2delta+eta, 3delta+eta, the scale by M, and the count of M=T/r products.

G1 states P_sF_s = 2^{2alpha^2} B_0 P_t F_t A, the error p^2, the time O(tp^{3/2+delta} alpha) and the tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2. The sub-steps follow 3576-3696 (||N-I|| < 2^{-alpha^2 theta}, Neumann inversion, S', J', D' normalizations, the ordered selection C, permutations kept instead of sorts) and 3836-3889 (linewise padded box, error dp^2, axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau))).

H1 and H2 state eq:permuted-chirp and eq:source-permutation-cancel. The sub-steps reproduce periodicity for even t_i, the coefficient comparison, F_q^+ R_c = R_c^{-1} F_q^+, R F_s^+ R = F_s^+, the commutation with pointwise products, the two normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2, and conjugation.

PB.1 and PB.2 give the fixed exponents and sizes, and Q1 the prime intervals with eta=1/(4d), T/2<S<T and alpha^4 theta_i > p. Q1.1-Q1.5 follow 4110-4171 (Rosser-Schoenfeld via HvdH Lemma 5.1, disjoint intervals, Bernoulli, alpha^4 theta_i > 3db >= p, and a search in n^{o(1)}). gamma=2d alpha^2 appears in G1.9 and gamma <= b/4 in ER.9. The absence of wraparound is only mentioned (M0).

Q2 states the isomorphism x -> prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular digits b_i and the cost O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)). The sub-steps follow the order argument, the reason for the triangular formula, padding, the update order i=d..1, the bijection on the padded box, and the cost of offsets and axis reversal.

X1.1-X1.3 reproduce the well-definedness of x_d -> zeta y, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h = zeta^j, and M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = (f*g)/T. X1.4 gives the computed sequence. ER.2 gives the phase-product error below 4h_p.

X0.1-X0.3 give the chirp construction, the computed chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = R F_s, and the conjugated opposite procedure. M1-M6 give the six steps (digits scaled by 2^{-b-2}, Phi, two transforms, product, F~+ with scale S, scale 2^{2b+4}S, rounding, Phi^{-1}, carries). M7 explains the two occurrences of S.

The error chain E_ring < 5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s = 9*2^gamma TL, E_w < 28*2^gamma T^2 L and the final error < 448b 2^{-b+gamma} <= 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2 are all present, together with the disk margins, the rounding and the carry recurrence. ER.7's justification of 3E_s+2 omits one E_s term (see errors), but the stated bound is the paper's.

PB.4/PB.5 give the margins g_1..g_7 with their values and min g_i = g_2 = eps c(1-tau) = 2^{-181} = 2kappa. PB.6-PB.11 justify each row of the table as at 4857-4911. PB.12 covers setup and the exceptional-stream sorting, o(V). PB.13/PB.14 absorb the log factors and the small cutoff, giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}).

S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It never says what an eventual lower bound would require (T_A(n) >= c_A n lg n for large n) or that one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0 refutes it.

errors.says: Method: build the exchange from three stages, each a forward invocation y_S <- y_S + x_S.
errors.paper: Only stages 1 and 3 are forward invocations from X to Y. Stage 2 runs the inverse forward schedule from Y to X, which effects X <- X - Y; the chain (x,y) -> (x,y+x) -> (-y,y+x) -> (-y,x) depends on this. N0.4 states it correctly.

errors.says: In both networks the sum over all edges of the label-dimension changes equals Wm-2N+2L.
errors.paper: The signed changes sum to Wm-2N. Only the sum of absolute changes equals Wm-2N+2L. R0's method and R0.2 say this correctly.

errors.says: The controlled update y -> y+a (mod q^b), or multiplication by a fixed rational unit, costs O(V) because the update is a cyclic shift of blocks done by one split and merge; no condition is placed on the offset.
errors.paper: The O(V) bound requires that the offset be preparable in b^{O(1)} time from the controls. Unit multiplication is not a single split and merge: it uses c increasing pieces with a residue-counter merge, and negation uses a stack reversal.

errors.says: Method: the complex phase network's edge frames are products of two-point kernels on groups of f=e/m axes, so that each edge costs one smaller layer.
errors.paper: An edge costs one child call per vector in an orthonormal basis of its residual, rho_edge calls on that edge, so a node makes s_c calls in all. Y0 and Y0.4 state this correctly.

errors.says: The error before the scale by S is below (3E_s+2)h_p, since the product terms contribute at most 2E_s h_p, truncation adds 2h_p, and G = R F_s^+ is a contraction.
errors.paper: The listed contributions give only (2E_s+2)h_p, through ||G(z - U.V_1)||. The third E_s is the opposite procedure's own approximation error ||F~+(z) - Gz||, which the step omits.

chain: The tree reaches the main bound by the paper's route. Chunk interchange is built from the bit network, frames, labels, rank budget, matrix shear and recurrence. Butterfly layers come from the phase network, packed row additions, the layer recurrence and guard widths. Above these sit the synthetic transforms, signed packing and convolution, then Gaussian resampling with the retained permutations, the chirp and permutation cancellation, CRT, the multiplication algorithm, exact recovery and the margin table. Each step is backed by the paper's lines. The tree thins out only at the label construction: L0.4 restates, rather than derives, that the central 3->4 edges are the only decreases (the gate-label and residual tables are absent), and the binary orthonormal bases are asserted. The network's size parameters (h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3, the wire counts) are never stated, although the quantities derived from them (100/539, m<2^20) are.

steps.note: The fixed linear network is stated and derived: (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a), a plain swap over F_2, with every scratch wire restored by the subtract-first eight-row schedule over three stages. L0 gives triples and m=h^3. The parameter values are missing: h=100 is never stated, and N=binom(h,3)^3 is used but never defined. The verdict rests on the mechanism, which is complete.

Present: a common invertible frame per gate commuting with the pointwise gate, the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, and edges costing only the change D_v D_u^{-1}. In K0.2 this is applied with the shear frames Phi_M.

L0 states nondegenerate labels in F^{tensor 3} of dimension m, nested labels on every edge, and the central edges from time 3 to 4 as the only decreases, each losing h. Why the central edges lose P tensor F (the gate-label table) is asserted, not shown.
B0.1: rank(P_V - P_U) = dim V - dim U for nested nondegenerate labels, so the edge cost equals the dimension change. B0.2: the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a}, each of rank one.
R0.1/R0.2: signed changes Wm-2N, absolute total Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich. B0.2: s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b. R0's own sentence omits the word 'absolute' (listed as a minor error), but R0.2 supplies it.
R0.3 gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2. B0.3 gives the deficit N-2L_b > 0, hence s_b < W_b m, and P0.5 gives the complex deficit.

B0.4: M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m on all roles, via P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} = I_m and zero/identity for the other roles. K0.2: the frames make the output Phi_{I_m} f_w, i.e. H <- H+D on every row, including scratch rows.
T0/MS0: A = E_1 Pi E_2, with the rank-a shear costing exactly a interchanges plus O(V) (MS0.4 gives the three-step realization). PR0.1: a node makes exactly s recursive calls.

Children of volume V/W (K0.1, PR0.2). F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) (PR0.3), solved to O(e^tau) (PR0.4/PR0.5). B0.5 derives s/W < m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from deficits above 20*2^{-50} and m<2^20, i.e. log m<20.

central.summary: All nine steps of the central saving are reconstructed, in order and in their roles: the bank-exchange network, frames, labels, rank equal to dimension change, the budget Wm-2N+2L with s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b, the strict saving from L/N = 100/539 < 1/2, the endpoint identity giving H <- H+D, rank-a shears as a recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau = 1-2^{-50}. The weak points are that h=100 and N=binom(h,3)^3 are never stated, and that the label assignment behind the decreasing central edges is asserted rather than shown.
